body:
## Summary

Reuse one lazily created `MessageChannel` per synchronous import-index writer to yield to a posted-message task after the existing 6 ms active-work budget. Fall back to `setTimeout(0)` if `MessageChannel` is unavailable or cannot post, and close both ports after queued writes drain.

## Validation

- `npx vitest run test/term-record-import-index-writer.test.js test/term-record-import-index-flush.test.js` — 29 passed.
- `npx eslint ext/js/dictionary/term-record-import-index-writer.js test/term-record-import-index-writer.test.js` — passed (with the existing pako CommonJS-in-ESM warning).
- `npm run test:ts:main` and `npm run test:ts:test` — passed.

## Component timing

On Node 22, the production writer was forced through 20 task yields per sample using the same writer and file path. Across 21 samples, the old timer yield measured best 20.036 ms / median 23.677 ms; the reusable MessageChannel path measured best 0.074 ms / median 0.138 ms. Each sample posted 20 messages over one reused channel. This is phase-local evidence, not a whole-import claim.

No JMdict archive was present in the local cache, so a real JMdict import and browser timing were not run.
title: perf: use message tasks for import index yields
